description: Lint a chart specification for graphical integrity, in the tradition of Edward Tufte (The Visual Display of Quantitative Information) and Alberto Cairo (How Charts Lie). Pass `spec` as a JSON object or JSON string with: type (bar, column, line, area, pie, donut, scatter, bubble), title, source, units, labels (categories), series (list of {name, values, axis?}), axis {min, max, label}, axis2 {min, max} or dualAxis, threeD, stacked, sizeEncoding (area, radius, diameter, width, volume), decoration (list or object naming gradient, shadow, pattern, texture, heavyGridlines, border, backgroundImage, pictograph, ornament), valuesArePercent. Checks: clipped data, non-zero bar or area baselines with the lie factor (size of the effect shown in the graphic divided by the size of the effect in the data) computed from your first series, zoomed line axes, size encodings that scale by radius or volume (with the drawn ratio worked out), 3D, decoration that lowers the data-ink ratio, pies with more than about five slices or negative values, stacked or multi-line overload, dual axes, and a missing title, source or units. Each finding has an id, severity (error, warn, info), plain explanation and the numbers behind it. Pure computation: nothing is stored or logged.
